html:
The white church of a Benedictine monastery on the island of San Giorgio, across the water from Piazza San Marco in Venice, designed by Andrea Palladio. Doge Tribuno Memmo gave the island to the Benedictines in 982. Their church was rebuilt after an earthquake in 1223, and in 1565 the monks asked Palladio, who was already rebuilding their refectory, for a model of a new one. The first stone was laid in 1566.

The front is Palladio's answer to an old problem: how to give a church with a tall nave and low aisles the front of a classical temple. He laid two temple fronts over each other, a wide low one across the aisles and a tall narrow one, with giant columns, over the nave. The bright white interior joins a long nave to a cross plan with transepts. Beside the high altar hang two large paintings by Tintoretto, the Last Supper and the Jews gathering manna in the desert.

The body of the church was finished by 1575. Palladio died in 1580; the choir was built to his design by 1589, and the front, begun in 1599, was completed to his model in 1610. The bell tower fell in 1774 and was rebuilt by 1791.
